messages.subject: PD report not working
parts:
I am trying to convert my data into the MSStatsTMT format but I get an error suggesting that my annotation file names are not correct. Bellow you can find a reprex. I am only using two of my TMT channels since I only want to compare these down the line. I suspect that this is the problem. The two channels are part of an 18plex TPP experiment and I want to only compare the reference conditions of the treatment and control to see if at the standard temperature there are already stability changes upon treatment. 

If I should go about this differently suggestions are welcome!


``` r

library(MSstatsTMT)

library(tidyverse)


test2 <- raw.pd %>% select(-starts_with("Abundance"), "Abundance..126", "Abundance..131")

test3 <- annotation.pd %>% filter(Channel %in% c("126", "131"))


test5 <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(test2, test3)

#> INFO  [2024-01-31 23:05:16] ** Raw data from ProteomeDiscoverer imported successfully.

#> INFO  [2024-01-31 23:05:16] ** Raw data from ProteomeDiscoverer cleaned successfully.
```

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: PD report not working
parts:
Hi Jan-Philipp,

I will let others to comment on the format, but you are likely correct, this is likely due to a subsetting of the channels.

We do not recommend to subset the channels at the input stage. Even if you are not interested in comparing the other conditions, the remaining channels are useful for QC, and also for estimating the overall variability. A better workflow would be to use all the channels, and then compare the subset of conditions of interest using custom contrasts. See section 'MSstatsv4.0 Provides a Flexible Framework for Comparing Conditions'  in this manuscript.

I hope this helps at least somewhat
OV

Global median normalized peptide intensities:

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: PD report not working
parts:
Hi Jan-Philipp,

I am not sure what happens with the global median normalization (I will let others comment on this) but it is definitely not a good thing to do for TPP. I would set it to false.

Regarding the multi-plex comparison: indeed, if you use one channel as a reference (i.e., you equalize protein summaries in this channel between the plexes), then you can no longer use the channel for the downstream statistical analysis. This is because the normalization removes the variability in this channel. So my advice is to use another channel as the reference if possible (i.e., you assume that in that channel, there are no biological reasons for changes in protein abundance). If this is not possible and you want to proceed with the comparison, you can try reducing the peptide ions to a subset that is present in every plex. But  this is not great, as you will both lose many proteins and lose statistical power. Overall, having the right controls in a multi-plex TPP experiment goes the longest way.

HTH
OV
